cands.name: Forrest Satterfield

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Huntsville engineer and entrepreneur with a UAB biomedical engineering degree. Founded Satterfield Technologies at 19 and Obex Health, which made custom-fit N95 masks. Co-founded Cicada, a civic-tech company. Works as a manufacturing data scientist. Democratic nominee for Alabama House District 21 in 2026. Has held no public office.

endorsements.text: Tabitha's List: Candidates You Can Trust (Sway voting group), listed as an endorsement or voter guide recommendation on Ballotpedia
Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy (Sway voting group), listed as an endorsement or voter guide recommendation on Ballotpedia
For The Future Victory Fund, shown as an endorsement on his campaign site

cands.gaps: We found no public record of Satterfield holding any elected or appointed office, so there is no voting record to report. We found no bills sponsored and no official actions. We found no statements from him about data centers, homestead property taxes, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, police funding, gun laws, or abortion. We found no documented stance on development, no controversies and no foreign ties. His birthplace, upbringing and Alabama roots come from his own statements, which we could not check against an independent record such as a birth record or news profile. His employer is named as Leidos only in his Ballotpedia survey, and his campaign site describes it as a Huntsville defense and engineering company. We have no independent confirmation of his business claims, such as the Obex Health awards or the UAB startup history.

qual.background: Founded Satterfield Technologies (2014), launched Obex Health in 2020, and joined gener8tor to build a medical-bill auditing company. Later consulted, then became a Manufacturing Data Scientist at Leidos. Co-founded Cicada, a civic-tech company whose tools explain state bills and show how legislators voted. No elected office or legislative work.
qual.why: He has real business founding and management experience plus data and engineering work, which fits the middle band. He has no legislative service and no law, policy-staff or budget career.
qual.label: He has real business founding and management experience plus data and engineering work, which fits the middle band. He has no legislative service and no law, policy-staff or budget career.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says he would push for competitive teacher pay and raise starting teacher salaries. He gave no stated position on vouchers, charters or school choice in the pages reviewed.

land-for-floridians.evidence: His campaign site says his plan includes protecting homes from Wall Street. The page gives no details on limits for institutional, foreign or out-of-state buyers.

cands.name: Rex Reynolds

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives for District 21 since a March 2018 special election. Former Huntsville director of public safety and city administrator (until 2013). Owner of Reynolds Consulting Services, LLC, and later president and COO of Sharp Communication.
cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Rex Reynolds was born or raised, or when he moved to Alabama. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, guns, abortion, schools, policing or donor money, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. The pages we had did not list specific bills he sponsored or any actions he took on these issues. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties, or endorsements for him. The Wikipedia page was nearly empty.
